sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and path helpers
sections.what: Imports the SQLite library, path tools, and the two helpers that build native paths and read-only addresses.
sections.why: Lets the tests create databases and open them the same way the app does.

sections.name: test_literal_special_characters_and_native_paths_remain_readonly
sections.title: Read-only open with special characters
sections.what: Creates a database with a table holding one value, then opens it read-only, once with a normal path and once with a native path. It checks that the value can be read and that inserting a new row fails with a readonly error.
sections.why: Likely reason: file names with symbols and Windows path forms are common in real use, and the read-only guard must still hold for them.
sections.watch_out: The check relies on the error text containing readonly, which depends on the SQLite version.

sections.name: test_missing_readonly_database_is_not_created
sections.title: Missing read-only database is not created
sections.what: Tries to open a missing database in read-only mode, checks that an error is raised, and confirms the file was not created.
sections.why: Likely reason: a read-only open should never create a new empty database that could later be mistaken for real data.
sections.watch_out: If the read-only address is changed to allow creation, this test will fail and should be treated as a real regression.

summary: Checks that SQLite database files can be opened read-only even when their path has special characters or uses the native Windows path form, and that a missing read-only database is not created.
purpose: Protects saved schedule databases from being changed or created by accident when the app only needs to read them.
why: Likely reason: special characters in a path can break the database address, and a read-only open is a safety step that must keep working for odd paths.
how: One test creates a database whose name includes symbols such as hash, percent and ampersand, then opens it through a read-only address both as a normal path and as a native path. It checks that reading works and that writing fails. Another test checks that opening a missing read-only database raises an error and creates no file.
inputs: Temporary database files created in the test folder.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The tests create only temporary files.
risks: The tests check error text containing the word readonly, which can change between SQLite versions. The native path form is only truly exercised on Windows.
debug: If a test fails, print the readonly address that readonly_uri returns for the failing path. Check whether the special characters were encoded and whether native_path changed the separators.
